assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength lattice proposal and Ye's demonstration of very high stability and accuracy with strontium, opened a new regime of precision measurement. The work depends on detailed atomic-structure understanding (polarizabilities, blackbody shifts, clock transitions), which I can judge well from the atomic-physics side. Applications include tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: The magic-wavelength concept is clearly credited to Katori, and Ye's JILA group brought the clocks to the 1e-18 level. Both can be named as a coherent two-person configuration. Other strontium and ytterbium groups (and earlier ion-clock work already recognized in 2012 and 2005) are contributors, but the supplied credit supports a clean pair.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty years of independent confirmation across many laboratories and species, with an established route to a redefinition of the second. Recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: How a committee would weigh this against the 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (ion control) prizes in the same precision-measurement lineage.
Whether other early lattice-clock contributors, which the list does not credit, have a competing claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned the Hubbard model into a controllable laboratory system: the Mott insulator transition, single-site quantum gas microscopes and quantum simulation of many-body dynamics. It is a conceptually clear, original bridge between atomic physics and condensed matter and many-body theory, and has lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposals; Bloch and Greiner carried out the decisive Mott-insulator experiments and built the field. Cirac is a strong theorist, but a three-person split of theory plus the two leading experimental demonstrations is defensible; the four credited names cannot all be included. Greiner's microscope work and Bloch's wider programme overlap, and Jaksch is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed by many groups; quantum gas microscopy and simulations are now routine. Some quantum-simulation claims of advantage are still evolving, but the foundational discoveries are stable.
uncertainties: Division of credit between theorists (Zoller, Cirac) and experimentalists, and omission of Jaksch from the supplied names.
Whether the 2001 BEC and 2012 prizes already cover enough of the ultracold-atom landscape.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field. It is original, has a clear mechanism and has changed condensed matter research widely.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observation. This is a natural theory plus experiment configuration. Other groups (for example early related transport work) may have claims that the supplied names do not cover.
assessment.maturity: Eight years of broad independent confirmation, though the origin of superconductivity and the correlated phases is not fully settled. The discovery itself is robust, but the interpretation of the physics is still debated, which makes the timing arguably early.
uncertainties: Unresolved pairing mechanism for the superconductivity.
Possible attribution to other contributors, such as work on moire flat bands before 2018, which the supplied credit does not include.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases, from the Aharonov-Bohm effect to Berry's adiabatic phase, form a unifying concept across quantum mechanics, molecular physics, optics and topological matter. The concept is original and its scope is very wide, including in atomic and molecular systems that I work on.
assessment.attribution: A clean two-person configuration is available: Berry for the adiabatic phase, Aharonov for the Aharonov-Bohm and Aharonov-Anandan work. Aharonov-Bohm is also credited to Bohm (deceased) and earlier to Ehrenberg and Siday, and Pancharatnam, Simon and Wilczek-Zee have claims that are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature and confirmed in many experiments, so the issue is not maturity. A prize may feel late, and some argue the concept is more a framework than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel statutes' emphasis on a discovery or invention is satisfied by a conceptual framework.
Credit disputes involving deceased or uncredited contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave photons, and underpins superconducting quantum processors. The importance and experimental clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the architecture, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. The three names support a theory plus two-experiment configuration, though Devoret, Martinis and Clarke were recognized in 2025 for related circuit physics and the boundaries may overlap.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and highly reproduced. The relationship to the 2025 prize could make a prize in the same area soon seem too close.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits.
Whether practical quantum computing impact is considered separately from the physics discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution, from BB84 to the entanglement-based Ekert protocol, links fundamental quantum theory to secure communication and is original and conceptually clear. It is now commercially and experimentally realized.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the natural BB84 pair and Ekert the entanglement-based proposal; Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not credited and he cannot be added. The three-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mature in experiments, but the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests already recognized closely related foundations. Practical security loopholes are still active research.
uncertainties: Whether recognition of a protocol proposal, rather than a physical discovery, fits the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays of optical tweezers realized controllable many-body quantum simulators and gates, drawing on blockade physics and atomic structure that I know well. It is highly active and important.
assessment.attribution: Lukin, Browaeys and Saffman each made major contributions, including Saffman's blockade-gate proposal and the experimental array demonstrations; however, other groups (for example Bloch, Ahn, Regal in tweezers) are not in the supplied credit and the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly developing and still evolving; independent confirmation is substantial, but the long-term impact is not yet fixed. This is likely early.
uncertainties: Prematurity relative to the field's trajectory.
Competing claims about who invented the key tweezer-array and blockade techniques.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened neutrino astronomy and was followed by source association with a blazar and the Galactic plane. It is an original, clear observational breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Only Halzen is credited, but IceCube is a large collaboration; a prize to one person would underrepresent the contributions of others and the statutes allow at most three. This is the main attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been independently supported by ANTARES-like and other analyses and by multimessenger observations; the maturity is reasonable, though source identification is still partial.
uncertainties: Credit allocation within a large collaboration.
Only one name is supplied, limiting a fair configuration.
